question: In real research reading, scholar will search for relavent work or follow-up papers in order to get a more comprehensive understanding. Is there any work done to automate or assist in this process?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: Answer affirms that relevant work exists, scoped to digital-resolution biomolecular sensing and liquid biopsy for diagnostics and life-science research.
examples: Yes — substantial work exists, exemplified by digital PCR-based ctDNA studies and reviews of digital resolution sensing
Yes, this frontier has been pursued in biosensing and liquid biopsy research

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: Answer summarizes the critical review: quantifying target molecules with enough precision to count individual units, observe individual biomolecular interactions, characterize binding kinetics, and quantify molecules in complex specimens.
examples: Counting individual target molecules in a test sample
Ultra-sensitive limits of detection for in vitro diagnostics
Digital precision enables observation of individual biomolecular interactions

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: Answer cites the 640-patient digital PCR study on non-invasive ctDNA tumor detection, including detectability rates across cancer types and stages (e.g., >75% in advanced pancreatic, ovarian, colorectal; ~48-73% in localized cancers; <50% in primary brain, renal, prostate, thyroid).
examples: ctDNA detectable in >75% of advanced pancreatic, ovarian, and colorectal cancers
Detection rates differ by cancer type and tumor localization

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: Answer defines liquid biopsy as analysis of circulating tumor cells or cell-free DNA in blood/body fluids and lists clinical applications such as early detection, post-surgery risk assessment, therapy monitoring, and resistance mechanism discovery.
examples: Liquid biopsy analyzes CTCs or cell-free DNA in blood
Identification of patients at high risk for progression after curative surgery
Applications include early detection and monitoring disease progression

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: Answer reports the KRAS mutation detection performance from the 206-patient metastatic colorectal cohort: 87.2% sensitivity and 99.2% specificity.
examples: Sensitivity of 87.2% and specificity of 99.2% for clinically relevant KRAS mutations
High specificity makes ctDNA a reliable mutation detection tool

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: Answer covers the EGFR-blockade relapse cohort finding that 96% (23/24) of relapsed patients acquired MAPK-pathway mutations revealed through ctDNA sequencing.
examples: 23 of 24 relapsed patients developed MAPK pathway mutations
ctDNA provides clues into resistance to EGFR blockade

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: Answer notes that ctDNA was often present in patients without detectable circulating tumor cells, indicating the two are distinct biomarker entities.
examples: ctDNA detectable even without circulating tumor cells
The two biomarkers are distinct

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: Answer explains the clinical motivation that metastatic spread through the blood is the main cause of cancer-related death, making blood a key diagnostic fluid.
examples: Colonization of distant organs is the main cause of cancer death
Blood is an important fluid for diagnostic exploration

ingredients.name: valuable_3
ingredients.criterion: Answer connects digital precision sensing to deeper insight into biological processes through observation of individual biomolecular interactions, beyond clinical diagnostics.
examples: Observing individual molecular binding events yields biological insight
Greater precision in characterizing biomolecular binding kinetics
